text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Four people feared dead in city floods.
- Police unearth a firearms-smuggling syndicate in Nairobi.
- A young man in the Rift Valley in selling one his kidneys to pay for his college studies.
- Opposition parties angry over police beating of opposition leader Raila Odinga on Saturday.
- A young millionaire behind a forgeries factory goes underground.
- Local musicians appeal to Kenya Broadcasting Corporation to reconsider playing vernacular music on the national service.
- Opposition leader George Anyona says the expulsion threat issued to members of the Asian community by opposition leaders Raila Odinga and Kenneth Matiba is a disastrous political stunt.
- Police in eastern Kenya recover 10,400 head of cattle stolen by cattle rustlers.
- Roman Catholic bishops from across Africa are in Nairobi for an emergency meeting on the Great Lakes crisis.
- A directive by the Kenyan government to abolish the post of executive chairman in all state corporations is shelved amid fears it might be misunderstood ahead of elections.
- The Ugandan govenment ban on cigarette imports stays. ($1=54 Kenyan Shillings)
